mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the past month signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL annualized growth exceeds 2% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the past three months signals a tightening labor market, which leads to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5pp in 3 months and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the past two months signals increased economic activity and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases by more than 5% in 2 months and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the past two months signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO decreases by more than 1% in 2 months and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) growth is below 1% annualized, it signals a mismatch between monetary policy and inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL annualized growth < 1% and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the past three months signals robust consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases over three months and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 over the past month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3 percentage points, it signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.3pp in 1 month
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.3pp in 1 month and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) growth is negative for two consecutive months and GDP (GDPC1) growth is below 1% annualized, it signals a supply-side recession, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO negative for 2 months and GDPC1 annualized growth < 1%
failure_condition: If INDPRO is negative for 2 months and GDPC1 annualized growth < 1% and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.
